name: Combustion of mixed organics
description: This process reflects the Combustion of Mixed Organics normalized to the functional unit of 1 short ton of treated waste. This process was adapted from WARM v16 zolca format.
category: 56: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services/5622: Waste Treatment and Disposal

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Data providers and sources range in age (e.g. 1990s-2010s).
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This process represents an average US combustion under average conditions. Includes collection, transport, combustion of waste, energy recovery in the electric utility sector and recovery of ferrous metals.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: National average mass burn and transport data.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Data from WARM v16 in openLCA (zolca) format was adapted to be compatible with the Federal LCA Commons. This included mapping the elementary flows to the Federal Elementary Flow List and mapping background technosphere flows (e.g., transport, fuels, and electricity) to existing USLCI flows. Steel recycling and credits associated with avoided steel are not included within this inventory. More information about the data transformation from WARM is provided here - https://github.com/FLCAC-admin/uslci-content/tree/dev/docs/supporting_docs/WARM. The amount of ash going to landfill post combustion was adapted from the WARM model to fix inconsistencies. The fraction of waste to ash is from the Municipal Solid Waste Decision Support Tool (MSW-DST). For mixed MSW, the composition of the waste is based on Facts and Figures 2018 for the ash calculations. (e.g., material 1 ash fraction from MSW-DST * fraction of material 1 in MSW from MSW-DST)
processDocumentation.completenessDescription:
Treatment of Missing Environmental Data: This process includes an inventory of direct greenhouse gas emissions and economic flows. View the WARM documentation for more details about missing environmental data.


Treatment of Missing Technosphere Data: There are no major gaps in technosphere data. View the WARM documentation for more information.

Mass Balance: Mass balance calculations for this process are included in the background WARM documentation.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Inventory exchange values were generated based on sources cited in EPA documentation for the WARM model
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Inventory exchange values were generated based on sources cited in EPA documentation for the WARM model. View the modeling constants field above. More information about the data transformation from WARM is provided here - https://github.com/FLCAC-admin/uslci-content/tree/dev/docs/supporting_docs/WARM.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The combustion system is inclusive of collection, transport, combustion of waste, energy recovery in the electric utility sector and recovery of ferrous metals. Inventory exchange values were generated based on sources cited in EPA documentation for the WARM model. Uncertainty is not calculated.

reviews.details: WARM has been externally peer reviewed and this openLCA inventory was reviewed internally.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: EPA created the Waste Reduction Model to provide high-level comparisons of potential greenhouse gas emissions reductions, energy savings, and economic impacts when considering different materials management practices. WARM exclusively evaluates GHG and economic impacts of waste management pathways, and is intended as a purely descriptive model of the systems under analysis.
